report.answer_text:
DeepSeek-R1 was an AI reasoning model released by the Chinese startup DeepSeek on January 20, 2025. DeepSeek made the model’s weights publicly available and reported that R1 performed comparably to OpenAI’s o1 on several math, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. It also offered access to R1 at a much lower price than OpenAI charged for o1. (deepseek.com)
It shook tech stocks because it challenged assumptions about how much computing power—and money—companies needed to build competitive AI. Investors questioned whether tech giants would need to spend as much on advanced chips and data centers as expected, and whether established AI providers could keep charging premium prices. As DeepSeek’s app surged in popularity, the sell-off hit on January 27, 2025: Nvidia fell about 17%, losing roughly $590 billion in market value, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 3.1%. (investing.com)
One important distinction: the widely quoted $5.6 million was DeepSeek’s estimate for the computing cost of the official training runs for its earlier V3 model. It excluded prior research and experiments and was not the total cost of developing R1. The sell-off reflected a shift in investor expectations, not proof that demand for AI chips would fall. (sitelet.easiiodev.ai)
